claims.text: Accelerated coupled degradation in the multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy is driven by wear-induced removal of protective oxide layers.
Oxide removal exposes highly reactive phase boundaries that are susceptible to corrosion.
Repeated oxide removal produces an unsteady cycle of passivating-film formation and breakdown.
The oxide formation-and-breakdown cycle amplifies both wear and corrosion.
The initial alloy forms a relatively stable protective oxide layer under quiescent conditions.
Phase boundaries in the initial multiphase microstructure are potential sites for corrosion initiation.
Elevated temperature enhances oxidation dynamics.
Differences in oxidation kinetics among phases cause non-uniform oxide-film growth.
Non-uniform oxide growth creates local defects that become sites of accelerated degradation.
Wear mechanically strips the protective oxide film and exposes reactive phase boundaries.
Exposed phase boundaries rapidly form non-uniform oxides in a high-temperature corrosive medium.
Cyclic oxide formation and removal increases local stress concentrations and corrosion gradients.
The increased stress concentrations and corrosion gradients synergistically enhance both wear and corrosion damage.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion will produce a significantly higher total degradation rate than separate wear-only or corrosion-only exposure.
Simultaneous exposure will increase wear volume loss relative to the matched separate-exposure baseline.
Simultaneous exposure will produce deeper and more localized corrosion pits relative to the matched separate-exposure baseline.
The enhanced localized corrosion is caused by an inability of the substrate to re-establish a uniform protective oxide layer.
The mechanism applies when oxidation kinetics are fast and a protective oxide film can be mechanically disrupted.
The mechanism may not operate if the oxide is too robust or the corrosive medium is insufficiently aggressive.
A four-condition comparison comprising wear-only, corrosion-only, simultaneous wear and corrosion, and neither exposure can test the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The prediction compares simultaneous exposure with either separate wear-only or corrosion-only baselines, whereas the falsification rule requires simultaneous degradation to exceed the sum of both separate treatments. These are materially different synergy criteria, so a result could satisfy the stated prediction while failing the stated falsification test.
